titleInfo.title: Netscape time
titleInfo.subTitle: the making of the billion-dollar start-up that took on Microsoft

abstract.#text: "The inside story of the rise of the Internet. In Netscape Time, Jim Clark, cofounder and chairman of Netscape, recounts the tense, heady days when he and a group of programmers started a company that would change the face of business and communications for people around the world. Ever fearful of attracting the attention of the infinitely powerful Microsoft, Clark and his band of technology rebels worked day and night under incredible pressure to produce the first Internet browser, which ultimately enabled hundreds of millions of people to access the information superhighway."--Jacket.

tableOfContents.#text: We Have Liftoff Summer 1995 -- The Offering -- Trajectories Winter 1994 -- One Billion Is the Best Revenge -- Meeting Marc -- Getting to Go -- Operation Pied Piper -- Speed 2.0 -- Omens, Portents, Distant Thunder -- Into the Grinder -- The Vulcan Mind Meld -- Making a Business -- The Deal -- Creation and Confrontations Spring 1995 -- Jim Barksdale--The Right Stuff -- Staying Alive -- The Plea for Reason -- Run to Daylight Spring/Summer 1995 -- Breakaway -- Magnetars and Momentum -- The Decision -- The Best of Enemies -- Epilogue: The Long March at Double Time.

physicalLocation.#text: Baker Library, Harvard Business School, Harvard University
